    - Citizenship (if non-US citizen, you’ll need your USCIS document, such as your Permanent Resident Card, Employment Authorization Card, or Refugee Travel Document)

- You may also be able to attend school or training while receiving unemployment benefits. Learn more about California Training Benefits here: https://edd.ca.gov/en/unemployment/Eligible_Training_Types_for_CTB/ 
- Am I eligible? You need to have all of the following to get unemployment benefits: Social Security number, authorization to work in the US (if not a US citizen), have earned a minimum amount of money over the past 18 months (called base period), be totally or partially unemployed through no fault of your own, and be physically able to, available for and looking for work each week and ready / willing to accept work right away
- What documents you need to make applying faster: 
    - Personal Information (SSN, photo ID, other identity documentation like a W2 or bill)
    - Past 18 Months of Employment Information (Employer names, mailing and physical addresses, dates worked, total income before taxes and deductions (gross wages), hours worked, and how you were paid (e.g., weekly or monthly)
    - Most Recent Employer Information (Employer name, address, and phone number and your immediate supervisor, date you last worked, and total income before taxes and deductions (gross wages) in the last week (Sun - Sat) you worked
    - Reason you aren't working or had your hours cut (note: if you voluntarily quit or were fired / let go for misconduct, you may not be able to get benefits) 
    - Citizenship (if non-US citizen, you’ll need your USCIS document, such as your Permanent Resident Card, Employment Authorization Card, or Refugee Travel Document) 
    - There are additional documents if you worked in federal government or military service in the last 18 months (Notice to Federal Employee About Unemployment Insurance, Standard Form 8 and DD214 Member Copy 4 respectively). 

- How to apply and what to expect? 
**Step 1:** Get all the information and documents above together. 
**Step 2:** Apply online on California's EDD website, call by phone 1-800-300-5616 M-F 8am to 5pm PT or apply by fax or mail 
**Step 3:** After you apply, you have 21 days to sign up for and upload your resume to CalJOBS. 
**Step 4:** Review Benefit Documents - 2 weeks after you apply, California EDD may ask for more information. They will also send you key documents about your benefits. Details below: 
    - Notice of Unemployment Insurance Claim Filed (DE 1101CLMT): This is a summary of your claim information. It explains how to correct any errors to avoid payment delays.
Employment Development Department Customer Account Number Notification (DE 5614): This has your EDD Customer Account Number (EDDCAN) to register in UI Online, after you visit myEDD. The EDDCAN also helps verify your account if you speak with an EDD representative. Don’t lose it.
    - Notice of Unemployment Insurance Award (DE 429Z): This form explains what benefits you can expect, and how to avoid payment delays. If any information is wrong, follow the instructions and appeal in writing within 30 days to avoid payment delays.
Unemployment Insurance Benefits: What You Need to Know (DE 1275B): This provides you a link to a document that explains how you can avoid payment delays by accurately certifying for benefits every two weeks.
    - Continued Claim (DE 4581): You can use this form to certify by paper, but the process is much slower. Save time and do it online at myEDD or by phone. You’ll certify for benefits every two weeks.
    - Request for Identity Verification (DE 1326C): If you applied by phone, fax, or mail (or we can’t immediately verify your identity), you’ll receive this form. Visit Respond to Your Request for Identity Verification to learn how to avoid further delays.
**Step 5:** Certify for Benefits - you need to answer some basic questions every 2 weeks to tell EDD that you are still unemployed but actively looking. Keep an eye out for an email / mail from EDD when it's time. It's fastest to certify online through myEDD, but you can also call 1-866-333-4606 for English and Spanish or by mail (your payments may take longer by mail)
**Step 6:** Receive Your First Payment - generally takes 3 weeks after you submit your application up to getting your first payment. You can get it by direct deposit, debit card or mailed check. Note, there is a one week waiting period on your claim before getting paid. Your first certification will usually include one week unpaid waiting period and one week of payment if you meet eligibility for both weeks. 
**Step 7:** Keep Certifying - you must do this step 5 every 2 weeks to keep your benefits 
**Step 8:** End Your Benefits: your benefit year ends 12 months after the start date of your first claim. You will need to re-apply if you still meet eligibility criteria. 

California also offers a lot of options finding a new job: 
- Workshops and services to improve your resume and develop job search skills, see EDD's website for more: https://edd.ca.gov/en/jobs/ 
- If you apply for unemployment benefits, you also have to create an account with CalJOBS and can find: education and training programs, customize job searches, create different resumes, research employers, set up alerts, apply directly to any openings, and there is a mobile app to make things easier too. 
- America's Job Center of California (AJCC) also gives free job and training services. You can use the American Job Center Finder to find a AJCC near you. You can also attend job fairs and career workshops with the AJCC to help grow your network. You can also join local or virtual workshops on common topics like how to use CalJOBS, how to search for jobs, and resume tips and interview coaching. 

There are many programs in California that could help like SNAP or CalFresh for food, CalWORKs or TANF if you have kids at home too, and help paying rent or utilities, getting health coverage, financial planning support and more. Would you like to learn more about these?

You may qualify for **expedited CalFresh benefits within 3 days** if you meet any of these:
* Less than $150 in monthly gross income AND less than $100 in liquid resources
* Combined monthly income and resources less than rent/mortgage + utilities
* You are a migrant/seasonal farmworker with less than $100 in resources

## Income & Benefits Considerations
* **Unemployment Insurance (UI)** DOES count as income for CalFresh
* **Severance pay** counts as income in the month received
* Current income limits (family of 3): **$2,987/month** gross income

## Moving Counties
* Notify your current county office **before moving**
* Benefits can transfer between California counties
* Need to:
  * Update your address
  * Request case transfer to new county
  * Benefits continue without interruption if reported promptly

## Next Steps
1. **Apply immediately** through:
   * [GetCalFresh.org](https://getcalfresh.org)
   * Call 1-877-847-3663
2. **Request expedited processing** during application
3. Have ready:
   * ID
   * Proof of income/job loss
   * Rent/utility bills
   * Children's information

Sorry to hear you've lost your job and working through an appeal on top of that. The appeals process can be challenging, I'm here to help you navigate impacts to your benefits. Can you clarify which program decision you are appealing? Is it WIC or unemployment?

Appealing a decision for WIC would not affect your unemployment benefits and vice versa. These programs are run by different agencies in California. Unemployment Benefits is run by EDD or the Employment Development Department. And WIC is run by the CA Department of Public Health. 

## For unemployment appeals: 
It's important that you continue to certify for benefits every 2 weeks while your appeal is in progress. They can only pay you back for weeks you were eligible. If you do not keep certifying every 2 weeks, you won't get benefits for that time if the appeal decision is positive. 
The process after you file an appeal: 
- Do not reapply for unemployment while you are waiting for an appeal decision, this will likely delay your case further 
- The EDD needs time to review your appeal and why you think there is a mistake. 
- If the additional information you shared does not change EDD's decision, they will send your appeal to the California Unemployment Insurance Appeals Board (Office of Appeals). 
- The Office of Appeals will send you more information about the appeal process and will schedule a hearing to listen to your appeal and make a decision. 
- You'll get a Notice of Hearing by mail at least 10 days in advance. It will have the date, time, and location. For information about what to expect at your hearing and how to prepare, please visit the California Unemployment Insurance Appeals Board website.

## For WIC appeals: 
- You also should not reapply for WIC if you are waiting to hear back on an appeal. This will likely create issues in the system and delay the process for you. 
If your appeal is unrelated to WIC and you want to re-apply here are the steps you should take: 
WIC helps growing families pay for healthy foods and provides guidance on nutrition. 
Eligibility: You may qualify if you: 
- Are pregnant, breastfeeding or just had a baby or recent pregnancy loss in the last 6 months **or** have a child or care for a child under 5 years old **and**
- have low to medium income (earn less than 185% of the federal poverty level) or receive Medi-Cal, CalWORKS, or CalFresh **and**
- live in California

## WIC Application After Job Loss

**Good news**: Applying for WIC while having an appeal pending won't affect your unemployment benefits. Here's what you need to know:

## Required Documents
- **Proof of income loss** (termination letter or final pay stub)
- **ID** (California driver's license or state ID)
- **Proof of residence** (utility bill or lease)
- **Current unemployment award letter** (if receiving benefits)

## Important Timelines
| Action | Timeline |
|--------|----------|
| WIC Application Processing | 10-15 business days |
| Income Verification | Must be from last 30 days |
| Benefits Start | Can begin same day if expedited |
| Certification Period | Usually 6-12 months |

## Key Points
- Your unemployment benefits are **separate** from WIC and won't be affected
- You can have both an appeal and a new application simultaneously
- Report your current unemployment income on the new application
- [Find your local WIC office](https://m.wic.ca.gov/Clinics/ClinicSearch.aspx) for fastest service

- CalWORKs helps with cash to pay for rent, housing, food, clothing, medical payments, and utilities for families with at least one child in the home. Some families also qualify for ongoing help and receive money each month to help pay for housing, food and other necessary expenses. The sooner you apply, the sooner you'll hear back on if you qualify. 
- Services vary by county but in addition to cash aid can include housing support, employment help, child care, education, mental health, substance use support, and domestic abuse support 
- You don't to be a US citizen to get cash help. Certain non-citizens may be eligible, including children born in the US even if parents are not. Applying won't affect your immigration status. California does not volunteer information about your immigration status to the federal government. 
- The amount of help you could get depends on your family's income, household size, and any special needs. Since you are taking care of children, you may qualify for more help as well like General Assistance.
- If approved for cash aid, the monthly amount gets added to your EBT card (same as CalFresh) or can be directly deposited into a bank account. 
To Apply: 
You can apply at any Social Services office in the county you live in (https://www.cdss.ca.gov/county-offices) or apply online at BenefitsCal.com. Applying through your county also checks you for other programs as well such as General Assistance.
Once you have all your documents, applying should take 30-60 minutes. I can also provide a more detailed list of the documents you would need, but generally: ID, proof you live in California, money you recieve, expenses. 
Key Dates: your county will tell you the kinds of change you need to report and by when, but usually within 10 days.  To keep your benefits, your county will also reach out once a year but each program has different requirements. 

## Unemployment Benefits 
- What is it? Temporary income when you lose your job (or had hours reduced) through no fault of your own. 
- How much can I get? You get from **$40 to $450** each week, depending on how much you earned in the past 18 months. EDD has an Unemployment Benefit Calculator to help you estimate how much you might get before you apply. 
- How long does it take to hear back? It takes about three weeks to process your benefit application and make the first payment. 
- You may also be able to attend school or training while receiving unemployment benefits. Learn more about California Training Benefits here: https://edd.ca.gov/en/unemployment/Eligible_Training_Types_for_CTB/ 
- Am I eligible? You need to have all of the following to get unemployment benefits: Social Security number, authorization to work in the US (if not a US citizen), have earned a minimum amount of money over the past 18 months (called base period), be totally or partially unemployed through no fault of your own, and be physically able to, available for and looking for work each week and ready / willing to accept work right away
- What documents you need to make applying faster: 
    - Personal Information (SSN, photo ID, other identity documentation like a W2 or bill)
    - Past 18 Months of Employment Information (Employer names, mailing and physical addresses, dates worked, total income before taxes and deductions (gross wages), hours worked, and how you were paid (e.g., weekly or monthly)
    - Most Recent Employer Information (Employer name, address, and phone number and your immediate supervisor, date you last worked, and total income before taxes and deductions (gross wages) in the last week (Sun - Sat) you worked
    - Reason you aren't working or had your hours cut (note: if you voluntarily quit or were fired / let go for misconduct, you may not be able to get benefits) 
    - Citizenship (if non-US citizen, you’ll need your USCIS document, such as your Permanent Resident Card, Employment Authorization Card, or Refugee Travel Document) 
    - There are additional documents if you worked in federal government or military service in the last 18 months (Notice to Federal Employee About Unemployment Insurance, Standard Form 8 and DD214 Member Copy 4 respectively). 

- How to apply and what to expect? 
**Step 1:** Get all the information and documents above together. 
**Step 2:** Apply online on California's EDD website, call by phone 1-800-300-5616 M-F 8am to 5pm PT or apply by fax or mail 
**Step 3:** After you apply, you have 21 days to sign up for and upload your resume to CalJOBS. 
**Step 4:** Review Benefit Documents - 2 weeks after you apply, California EDD may ask for more information. They will also send you key documents about your benefits. 
**Step 5:** Certify for Benefits - you need to answer some basic questions every 2 weeks to tell EDD that you are still unemployed but actively looking. Keep an eye out for an email / mail from EDD when it's time. It's fastest to certify online through myEDD, but you can also call 1-866-333-4606 for English and Spanish or by mail (your payments may take longer by mail)
**Step 6:** Receive Your First Payment - generally takes 3 weeks after you submit your application up to getting your first payment. You can get it by direct deposit, debit card or mailed check. Note, there is a one week waiting period on your claim before getting paid. Your first certification will usually include one week unpaid waiting period and one week of payment if you meet eligibility for both weeks. 
**Step 7:** Keep Certifying - you must do this step 5 every 2 weeks to keep your benefits 
**Step 8:** End Your Benefits: your benefit year ends 12 months after the start date of your first claim. You will need to re-apply if you still meet eligibility criteria. 

## Help Finding a Job
- For workshops and services to improve your resume and develop job search skills, see EDD's website for more: https://edd.ca.gov/en/jobs/ 
- If you apply for unemployment benefits, you also have to create an account with CalJOBS and can find: education and training programs, customize job searches, create different resumes, research employers, set up alerts, apply directly to any openings, and there is a mobile app to make things easier too. 
- America's Job Center of California (AJCC) also gives free job and training services. You can use the American Job Center Finder to find a AJCC near you. You can also attend job fairs and career workshops with the AJCC to help grow your network. You can also join local or virtual workshops on common topics like how to use CalJOBS, how to search for jobs, and resume tips and interview coaching.  

California also has many options to help you with rent, utilities, and more when falling on hard times. Similar to the programs above, even if you are not a US citizen, help is still available if you can show proof of ID and since you are a legal resident. 

## Mortgage and Housing Help
Calling 2-1-1 in California is the best way to find help to pay your mortagage and utilities bills to stay in your home. Call to speak to someone right away. They will ask you a few questions about your current living situation, any income, any children or dependents who live with you. Even if you don't qualify for a government program, the state or local agency may refer you to a community organization or nonprofit in your area. 

If you're struggling to pay your mortgage, you should first talk with your lender to discuss your situation. There may be options like payment plans that could help you stay in your home. Don't stop paying your bills. Seek help early. If you want to talk to someone, the US Department of Housing and Urban Development offers a large network of housing counseling agencies that can help. Search for ones close to you here: https://answers.hud.gov/housingcounseling/s/?language=en_US 

It's important you know your rights. Protections against eviction and foreclosure vary by state: LawHelpCA.org  

If you are applying for or already get CalWORKS - California's TANF program - you may also be able to get help through their Housing Support Program or Homeless Assistance program if you are experiencing homelessness now or at risk. This program is run at the county level so contact them if you would like to learn more. Find shelters and temporary housing through HUD programs like their local homeless assistance list, their homeless continuing care program provider, and local public housing agencies: https://www.usa.gov/emergency-housing 

California also has programs to help with phone bills, low cost auto insurance, utilities / energy bills, and help with financial planning and debt. Do you want to learn more?

## Yes – You Can Apply for Multiple Programs at Once  

**Short answer:** In California you can receive several forms of assistance **simultaneously** (e.g., unemployment benefits, health coverage, food aid, and housing help). Each program has its own eligibility rules, but most are designed to work together.

---

## How Programs Coordinate

| Program | What It Covers | Typical Income/Asset Limits | Can It Be Combined With…? |
|---------|----------------|----------------------------|---------------------------|
| **Unemployment Insurance (UI)** | Weekly cash benefits while you’re looking for work | Must have earned enough wages in the base period; no strict income cap after you start receiving UI | **All other programs** (CalFresh, Medi‑Cal, rental assistance, etc.) |
| **CalFresh (SNAP)** | Monthly food benefits (EBT card) | Gross income ≤ 200 % of Federal Poverty Level (FPL); net income ≤ 100 % FPL after deductions | UI, SSI, SSDI, **Medi‑Cal**, housing assistance |
| **Medi‑Cal (California Medicaid)** | Free or low‑cost health coverage | Gross income ≤ 138 % of FPL (or higher for certain groups) | UI, CalFresh, **rent assistance**, other cash benefits |
| **California COVID‑19 Rental Assistance (CCRAP) / Emergency Rental Assistance (ERA)** | Grants to help pay rent & utilities | No strict income cap, but priority given to households ≤ 80 % of AMI | UI, CalFresh, **Medi‑Cal**, other cash assistance |
| **General Assistance (GA) / County Relief** | Cash aid for adults without other income | Varies by county; often ≤ 150 % of FPL | UI, CalFresh, **Medi‑Cal**, housing aid |
| **SSI/SSDI** | Federal disability benefits | Income limits apply; UI can be received concurrently (partial offset) | CalFresh, **Medi‑Cal**, housing assistance |

**Key point:** Most cash‑based programs (UI, GA, SSI) **do not disqualify** you from receiving non‑cash benefits (food, health, housing). The state’s “coordination of benefits” rules simply **adjust** the amount of cash you get so that total assistance stays within program limits.

---

1. **Gather Required Documents**  
   - Photo ID, Social Security number, proof of residence (utility bill or lease)  
   - Recent pay stubs or W‑2s (for UI)  
   - Bank statements (for CalFresh & GA)

   - File online at **[EDD UI Online](https://edd.ca.gov/Unemployment/UI_Online.htm)**.

3. **Apply for Health Coverage (Medi‑Cal)**  
   - Use **[Covered California](https://www.coveredca.com/medi-cal/)** or call 1‑800‑541‑5555.  
   - You can enroll **while UI is pending**; UI income is counted as “earned income” and is allowed.

|----------|--------|

- The California Women, Infants, and Children (WIC) program is a food and nutrition program for growing families. You can get help with nutrition education, breastfeeding and chestfeeding support, benefits to buy healthy foods, and referrals to health care and other community services. 

**Eligibility:**
You may qualify if you: 
- Are pregnant, breastfeeding or just had a baby or recent pregnancy loss in the last 6 months **or** have a child or care for a child under 5 years old **and**
- have low to medium income (earn less than 185% of the federal poverty level) or recieve Medi-Cal, CalWORKS, or CalFresh **and**
- live in California 

**How to apply**
Important: only staff at your local WIC can officially confirm if you qualify or not. 
Find a local WIC office near you: https://myfamily.wic.ca.gov/Home/WICOfficeGrocer#WICOfficeGrocer 

**Preparing for your WIC appointment**
- WIC staff may ask you bring your infant or child enrolling in the program to the WIC office

    - Proof of your family's household income (paycheck, tax return, letter from employer, Medi-Cal card)
    - Proof of pregnancy
    - Medical forms filled out by your health care provider

**What to expect at your first WIC appointment**
- A WIC counselor will determine if you are eligible for the program
- They will review the WIC program services and benefits with you 
- A nutrition assessment will also be completed for each member of your family who is eligible 
- WIC food benefits will be loaded onto the California WIC Card. 
- You can immediately use your WIC Card to purchase healthy foods.

1. **Identify your base period** (the first four of the last five completed quarters).  
2. **Find the quarter with the highest earnings** within that period.  
3. **Apply the 60 % rule** and compare the result to the $450 cap.  
4. **If the calculated amount is below $40**, you’ll receive the minimum $40 per week.

#### Example Calculation (2025)

| Quarter | Earnings | 60 % of Earnings | Weekly Benefit (rounded) |
|---------|----------|----------------|--------------------------|
| Q1 2023 | $5,200   | $3,120         | $60 (capped at $450)     |
| Q2 2023 | $4,800   | $2,880         | $55                      |
| Q3 2023 | $5,600   | $3,360         | $64                      |
| Q4 2023 | $5,000   | $3,000         | $57                      |

- **Highest quarter:** Q3 2023 → $5,600  
- 60 % of $5,600 = **$3,360**  
- Weekly benefit = $3,360 ÷ 52 ≈ **$64** (above the $40 minimum, below the $450 cap).

### Frequently Asked Questions

| Question | Answer |
|----------|--------|
| **Do I lose benefits if I start a part‑time job?** | No. UI benefits are **partial‑unemployment**; you can earn up to a certain amount each week (the “earnings disregard”) without a reduction. In 2025 the first $450 of earnings per week is ignored; any amount above that reduces your UI dollar‑for‑dollar. |
| **Can I receive UI if I have other income (e.g., freelance work, rental income)?** | Yes, as long as you meet the earnings‑history requirement. Other income may affect the weekly benefit amount through the earnings disregard rule. |
| **What if I don’t meet the $1,300 earnings threshold?** | You may still qualify for **Partial UI** if you earned at least $1,300 total in the base period, even if no single quarter reaches $1,300. |
| **Are there any “asset” limits (savings, investments)?** | No. California UI does **not** consider assets or net worth. |

### Next Steps for You

1. **Gather your recent pay stubs or W‑2s** for the last 12–18 months.  
2. **Use the EDD’s online UI calculator** to estimate your weekly benefit:  
   [EDD UI Benefits Calculator](https://edd.ca.gov/Unemployment/UI_Benefits_Calculator.htm)  
3. **File a claim** (you can start online, by phone, or at a local EDD office).  
4. **Keep a record of any earnings** while you receive UI, so you can report them accurately each week.

- Totally or partially unemployed.

- Physically able to work.
- Available for work.
- Looking for work each week.

Have reached the end of your benefit year.

Visit Tax Information (Form 1099G) for details.

**Maximum**: $73,000 (single) or $79,000 (married filing jointly). | | **Investment income** | Must be **≤ $11,000** for the year. | | **Qualifying children** | 0–3 children allowed. ## How Unemployment Insurance (UI) Works in California  

| Step | What Happens | What You Need to Do |
|------|--------------|---------------------|
| **1. Eligibility Check** | You must have earned enough wages during your “base period” (the first 4 of the last 5 completed calendar quarters) and be **unemployed through no fault of your own**. | Gather your **pay stubs**, **W‑2s**, or **DE 34/DE 35** wage reports from the last 12‑18 months. |
| **2. File a Claim** | The California Employment Development Department (EDD) processes your claim and assigns a **Weekly Benefit Amount (WBA)**. | File **online** at the EDD portal or call **1‑800‑300‑5616**. File **within 15 days** of your last workday to avoid losing benefits. |
| **3. Receive Weekly Payments** | Benefits are paid **weekly** (usually via direct deposit). You must certify each week you are still eligible. | Log in to **UI Online** each week, answer the certification questions, and report any earnings. |
| **4. Continue Job‑Search Requirements** | You must be **actively looking for work** and be able to accept suitable employment. | Keep a **record of at least 3 job contacts per week** (applications, interviews, networking). |
| **5. Benefit Duration** | Standard UI provides **up to 26 weeks** of benefits. Extensions may be available during high‑unemployment periods. | Check the EDD “**Extended Benefits**” page for current extensions. |

---

## How Your Weekly Benefit Amount (WBA) Is Calculated  

1. **Total your wages** in the base period.  
2. **Take the highest‑earning quarter** and divide by **26**.  
3. **Apply the minimum/maximum limits** (2025 figures):  

| Category | 2025 Amount |
|----------|------------|
| Minimum WBA | **$151** per week |
| Maximum WBA | **$1,357** per week |

### Example Calculation  

| Quarter | Wages Earned | WBA (Wages ÷ 26) |
|---------|--------------|------------------|
| Q1 (2023) | $9,800 | $376.92 |
| Q2 (2023) | $7,200 | $276.92 |
| Q3 (2023) | $5,500 | $211.54 |
| Q4 (2023) | $6,300 | $242.31 |

*Highest quarter = $9,800 → $9,800 ÷ 26 = **$376.92** → Rounded to **$377** weekly benefit.*

---

## Tips to **Maximize** What You Receive  

- **File Promptly** – Submit your claim within the 15‑day window after your last workday. Late filing can reduce the total number of weeks you’re eligible.  
- **Report All Earnings Accurately** – Even part‑time or gig work can be reported; the EDD will **adjust** your WBA for that week rather than disqualify you.  
- **Take Advantage of Partial Benefits** – If you work part‑time, you can still receive a reduced UI payment (earnings are deducted at a **75%** rate).  
- **Maintain Detailed Job‑Search Logs** – Keep dates, employer names, contact methods, and outcomes. This protects you during audits.  
- **Apply for Extensions Early** – If the state declares an **Extended Benefits** period, you must **re‑certify** and may need to submit a supplemental claim.  
- **Enroll in Re‑Employment Services** – The EDD offers **Work Opportunity Services (WOS)**, training, and resume workshops that can keep you eligible and improve job prospects.  
- **Check for Additional Programs** –  
  * **Pandemic Unemployment Assistance (PUA)** – expired in 2022, but similar emergency programs may appear.  
  * **Trade Adjustment Assistance (TAA)** – for workers displaced by foreign competition.  
  * **CalWORKs** – if you have dependent children and low income.  

---

## Step‑by‑Step: Filing Your Claim (Online)

1. Go to the **[EDD UI Online portal](https://edd.ca.gov/Unemployment/UI_Online.htm)**.  
2. Create a **Secure ID** (or log in with your existing ID).  
3. Select **“File a New Claim”** and answer the eligibility questions.  
4. Upload **wage documents** (pay stubs, DE 34/35).  
5. Choose **direct deposit** (bank account) for faster payments.  
6. Submit and note your **Confirmation Number**.  

*You’ll receive a **Benefit Claim Notice** within 2‑3 weeks with your WBA and start date.*

---

## Resources & Contacts  

| Resource | Link | What You’ll Find |
|----------|------|------------------|
| **EDD Unemployment Insurance** | [edd.ca.gov/Unemployment](https://edd.ca.gov/Unemployment) | General UI info, FAQs, and forms |
| **UI Online Portal** | [edd.ca.gov/UI_Online.htm](https://edd.ca.gov/UI_Online.htm) | Claim filing, weekly certification |
| **Benefit Claim Calculator** | [edd.ca.gov/Benefit_Calculator](https://edd.ca.gov/Benefit_Calculator) | Quick estimate of your WBA |
| **Job‑Search Log Template** | [EDD Job Search Log PDF](https://edd.ca.gov/Job_Search_Log.pdf) | Printable log to track contacts |
| **California Workforce Development Board** | [workforce.ca.gov](https://workforce.ca.gov) | Training programs, career counseling |
| **Phone – UI Claims** | 1‑800‑300‑5616 | Speak with an EDD representative (M‑F, 8 am‑5 pm PT) |
| **Live Chat** | Accessible via UI Online portal | Real‑time assistance during business hours |

---

## Quick Checklist Before You Submit  

- [ ] **Eligibility confirmed** (wages, reason for unemployment)  
- [ ] **All required documents** uploaded (pay stubs, DE 34/35)  
- [ ] **Bank account info** entered for direct deposit  
- [ ] **Job‑search log** ready for weekly certification  
- [ ] **Contact info** (phone, email) up‑to‑date  

---

**Remember:** UI benefits are a temporary safety net. Keeping your job‑search records current, reporting any earnings honestly, and staying on top of weekly certifications are the best ways to **protect and maximize** the assistance you receive. If you run into any issues, the EDD’s phone line and live chat are your first points of contact. Good luck, and feel free to ask if you need help with any specific step!

I'm sorry to hear that, job loss is very stressful especially with young children to take care of. Here are some options based on what you shared so far, I'm here to help. 

## Find Local Help 
- Findhelp.org is also a great search tool to find local resources near your zip code to find local food pantries, meal programs, and support for housing, financial assistance, health care, and more. Even if you don't qualify for public beneifts, there are still options for you in your community. 

## Food Help 
- If you need food now, you can go to Alameda County Community Food Bank 7900 Edgewater Drive Oakland or call first to see if you can get help: 510-635-3663
- You can also call 2-1-1 to get connect to resources any time 
- Apply for SNAP, called CalFresh in California. If eligible, you can get monthly help paying for groceries. It can take 30 days to hear back, but you can ask for faster help (expedited review). 
CalFresh Steps to Apply: 
- You can apply on BenefitsCal.com or go to your county office. Online chat support is available M-F 9am to 4pm PT. 
- Your county will call within 1-2 weeks for an interview and will let you know within 30 days if you're approved. 
- If approved, you will get your EBT card for groceries within 10 days. It gets refilled monthly. 
- Documents you need: copy of your ID, proof of any income, proof of immigration status (for non-citizens) within 30 days of applying. Other optional documents could increase you benefit amount like proof of housing expenses, child support, or dependent care.
- Contact your county CalFresh Office at 888-999-4772 for any questions or to follow up on your application 

Are any of your three kids under 5 years old? You may qualify for WIC (Women, Infants, and Children) program in California which provides additional cash aid to help with buying food and staying healthy. 

## Cash Aid (CalWORKs / TANF) 
- CalWORKs helps with cash to pay for rent, housing, food, clothing, medical payments, and utilities for families with at least one child in the home. Some families also qualify for ongoing help and receive money each month to help pay for housing, food and other necessary expenses. 
- Services vary by county but in addition to cash aid can include housing support, employment help, child care, education, mental health, substance use support, and domestic abuse support 
- The amount of help you could get depends on your family's income, household size, and any special needs. If you are taking care of your kids alone, you may qualify for more help as well. If you are a household of 4, living in Alameda County, you could get $1,412 (non-exempt) and $1,574 (exempt) 
- If approved for cash aid, the monthly amount gets added to your EBT card (same as CalFresh) or can be directly deposited into a bank account. 
To Apply: 
- You can apply at any Social Services office in Alameda County (https://www.cdss.ca.gov/county-offices) or apply online at BenefitsCal.com. There are multiple locations in Alameda County across Oakland, Hayward, Fremont, and Livermore. Feel free to search yourself or I can pull the address for you based on which location is closest. 
- Once you have all your documents, applying should take 30-60 minutes. I can also provide a more detailed list of the documents you would need, but generally: ID, proof you live in California, money you recieve, expenses. 

## Unemployment Benefits 
Cash aid from unemployment can also help make ends meet while you keep looking for a new job. 
- What is it? Temporary income when you lose your job (or had hours reduced) through no fault of your own. 
- How much can I get? You get from $40 to $450 each week, depending on how much you earned in the past 18 months. EDD has an Unemployment Benefit Calculator to help you estimate how much you might get before you apply. 
- How long does it take to hear back? It takes about three weeks to process your benefit application and make the first payment. 
- You may also be able to attend school or training while receiving unemployment benefits. Learn more about California Training Benefits here: https://edd.ca.gov/en/unemployment/Eligible_Training_Types_for_CTB/ 
- Am I eligible? You need to have all of the following to get unemployment benefits: Social Security number, authorization to work in the US (if not a US citizen), have earned a minimum amount of money over the past 18 months (called base period), be totally or partially unemployed through no fault of your own, and be physically able to, available for and looking for work each week and ready / willing to accept work right away
- What documents you need to make applying faster: 
    - Personal Information (SSN, photo ID, other identity documentation like a W2 or bill)
    - Past 18 Months of Employment Information (Employer names, mailing and physical addresses, dates worked, total income before taxes and deductions (gross wages), hours worked, and how you were paid (e.g., weekly or monthly)
    - Most Recent Employer Information (Employer name, address, and phone number and your immediate supervisor, date you last worked, and total income before taxes and deductions (gross wages) in the last week (Sun - Sat) you worked
    - Reason you aren't working or had your hours cut (note: if you voluntarily quit or were fired / let go for misconduct, you may not be able to get benefits) 
    - Citizenship (if non-US citizen, you’ll need your USCIS document, such as your Permanent Resident Card, Employment Authorization Card, or Refugee Travel Document) 
    - There are additional documents if you worked in federal government or military service in the last 18 months (Notice to Federal Employee About Unemployment Insurance, Standard Form 8 and DD214 Member Copy 4 respectively). 
- How to apply and what to expect? 
    - Step 1: Get Your Information in Order 
    - Step 2: Apply 
    - Step 3: Register in CalJOBS 
    - Step 4: Review Benefit Documents 
    - Step 5: Certify for Benefits 
    - Step 6: Receive Your First Payment 
    - Step 7: Continue to Certify

There are also many programs to help with utilities (lowering energy costs and help paying for energy bills), finding a job, phone bills, housing (rent or mortgage help), low cost auto insurance, affordable child care, and more. Would you like to hear more about any of these?

## Quick Answer  
**Yes – you can often receive both unemployment insurance (UI) benefits and Medi‑Cal at the same time**, but the amount you get and your eligibility will depend on:

| Factor | Effect on UI | Effect on Medi‑Cal |
|--------|--------------|--------------------|
| **Severance pay** | Treated as **wages** for the weeks it covers. UI benefits are delayed until the severance period ends. | Not counted as income **if it’s a one‑time lump‑sum** and you’re otherwise eligible. |
| **Part‑time gig earnings** | UI benefits are **reduced** by a portion of your earnings (usually 25 % of the amount over the weekly UI allowance). | Earnings are counted as **countable income**; you may still qualify if total household income stays below the Medi‑Cal limit. |
| **Weekly UI allowance (2025)** | $560 (average) – varies by prior wages. | Medi‑Cal income limit for a single adult: **~$1,500** per month (≈ $18,000 / yr). |

---

## 1. Unemployment Insurance (UI) in California  

### How Severance Impacts UI
- **Severance is considered wages** for the period it is meant to replace.  
- UI will **not be paid** for those weeks; benefits start **after the severance “cover period” ends**.  
- If your severance is a **lump‑sum** with no specific week‑by‑week allocation, you can **elect to treat it as a one‑time payment** and still claim UI immediately (you’ll just report it as “other income” on your claim).

### How Part‑Time Gig Work Impacts UI
| Gross weekly earnings | UI reduction (25 % of excess) |
|-----------------------|-------------------------------|
| $0 – $560 (full UI)   | $0 (no reduction)            |
| $560 – $1,120         | 25 % of amount over $560      |
| $1,120+               | UI may be eliminated          |

*Example:* If you earn $800 in a week, UI is reduced by 25 % × ($800 – $560) = $60. You’d receive **$560 – $60 = $500** in UI for that week.

### Reporting Requirements
1. **Every two weeks** when you certify your claim.  
2. List **all earnings** (including gig platform payouts, tips, and any severance you chose to treat as income).  
3. **Do not** hide income – the EDD cross‑checks with tax data and can penalize you.

### How to Apply / Check Status
- **Online:** [EDD UI Online Portal](https://edd.ca.gov/Unemployment/UI_Online.htm)  
- **Phone:** 1‑800‑300‑5616 (TTY 1‑800‑815‑9387)  

---

## 2. Medi‑Cal (California’s Medicaid)  

### Eligibility Basics (2025)
| Category | Income limit (monthly) | Notes |
|----------|------------------------|-------|
| **Single adult** | $1,500 | No dependents |
| **Couple (no children)** | $2,020 | Combined |
| **Family with children** | $2,500 + $150 per child | Up to 300 % of Federal Poverty Level (FPL) |

*These limits include **all** household income: wages, self‑employment, severance, unemployment, etc.*

### How Severance & UI Affect Medi‑Cal
- **Severance (lump‑sum)** is **counted as income** in the month you receive it. If it pushes you over the limit, you may be **temporarily ineligible** for that month but can re‑apply once the amount is “spent” (i.e., not counted in future months).  
- **UI benefits** are **countable income** but usually low enough to stay under the limit for most single adults.  

### How Part‑Time Gig Earnings Affect Medi‑Cal
- Add the **gross amount** you earn each month to your income total.  
- If you stay **below the monthly limit**, you keep full Medi‑Cal coverage.  
- If you exceed the limit, you may qualify for **Medi‑Cal Access (MCA)** – a reduced‑benefit program that still helps with most services.

### Applying for Medi‑Cal
- **Online:** [Covered California – Medi‑Cal Application](https://www.coveredca.com/medi-cal/)  
- **In‑person / Phone:** Call 1‑800‑541‑5555 or visit your local County Social Services Office.  

---

## 3. Putting It All Together  

### Step‑by‑Step Checklist
1. **Determine your severance structure**  
   - Lump‑sum → you can claim UI now (report as “other income”).  
   - Weekly/bi‑weekly → UI will be delayed until those weeks are covered.  

2. **Estimate weekly UI benefit** (use the EDD calculator).  

3. **Project your part‑time earnings**  
   - Use the table above to see how much UI will be reduced.  

4. **Add up monthly income** (UI + gig earnings + any severance counted that month).  

5. **Compare to Medi‑Cal limits** (see the table).  
   - If under the limit → you qualify for full Medi‑Cal.  
   - If slightly over → consider **Medi‑Cal Access** or **spending the excess** on allowable expenses (e.g., rent, utilities) before the month ends to lower countable income.  

6. **File both applications promptly**  
   - UI: within **one week** of your last workday.  
   - Medi‑Cal: as soon as you know your income picture; you can update the agency each month if your earnings change.  

### Tips for Success
- **Keep detailed records** of all gig payouts, tip reports, and severance statements.  
- **Report earnings accurately** on each UI certification to avoid overpayments and penalties.  
- **Ask for a “partial benefits” determination** if your earnings are modest; you’ll still receive a reduced UI amount.  
- **Use the “Income Exclusion” for certain expenses** (e.g., child support received, certain reimbursements) when reporting to Medi‑Cal.  
- **Consider a “budget plan”**: allocate a portion of your severance to a separate account to demonstrate it’s “spent” before the next Medi‑Cal eligibility review.  

---

## 4. Helpful Resources  

| Resource | Link |
|----------|------|
| **California Employment Development Department (EDD) – UI** | [edd.ca.gov/Unemployment](https://edd.ca.gov/Unemployment/) |
| **UI Benefits Calculator** | [EDD UI Calculator](https://edd.ca.gov/Unemployment/UI_Calculator.htm) |
| **Medi‑Cal Eligibility & Application** | [Covered California – Medi‑Cal](https://www.coveredca.com/medi-cal/) |
| **County Social Services Offices (find yours)** | [California Department of Social Services – County Offices](https://www.cdss.ca.gov/County-Offices) |
| **FAQ on Severance & UI** | [EDD Severance FAQ](https://edd.ca.gov/Unemployment/Severance_Pay.htm) |
| **Medi‑Cal Access (Reduced Benefits)** | [Medi‑Cal Access Info](https://www.cdss.ca.gov/medi-cal-access) |

---

## 5. Bottom Line  

- **You can receive UI while working part‑time**, but benefits will be reduced based on your earnings.  
- **Medi‑Cal is still available** as long as your combined monthly income (UI + gig earnings + any counted severance) stays under the program’s limit.  
- **Accurate, timely reporting** to both the EDD and Medi‑Cal is the key to keeping both benefits without interruption.  

If you need help filling out the applications or calculating your exact benefit amounts, feel free to ask!

## Health Care and Paying for Medical Bills 
For health coverage, California offers Medi-Cal or Medicaid which is free or low-cost health care to people who qualify. For those who make above Medi-Cal income limits, Covered California (state-based exchange to buy insurance through the Affordable Care Act) is another option to get help paying for a private healthcare plan. If your household does not have any income now that you've been laid off, you most likely qualify for Medi-Cal.  

### Medi-Cal Details
What Medi-Cal covers: pays for doctor visits, hospital care, immunization (vaccines), pregnancy related help, nursing home care and more

Eligibility: You have to live in California and meet certain rules like income cut-offs based on household size (138% of the federal poverty level or lower, which is $36,777 for a household of 3). If your aunt and uncle don't have any income either, then you most likely qualify for Medi-Cal. **Since your aunt has a disability, she may qualify for more help**. Even if your household income is over the Medi-Cal limit, you could still get help paying for private health care through Covered California. You can qualify even if you are not a US citizen or national.

- Go in person to your county office (if you tell me your county, I can look this up for you) or online on BenefitsCal.com.

### COBRA insurance 
You may have been offered temporary COBRA insurance, which is usually offered by your employer to help you keep your health plan after getting let go or getting reduced hours. You can still apply for Medi-Cal or Covered California even if you have a COBRA plan. It applies to most private companies with 20 or more employees. This depends on the qualifying life event. Some times this is 36 months or 3 years. If you are on COBRA because your employer reduced your hours or terminated your job, you could receive COBRA for 18 months or 1.5 years.

- A qualifying life event must occur

- Debt management: Get on a payment schedule with a credit counselor. You make an account with the credit counseling organization and then pay off your debt as you deposit money. You may get lower interest rates and certain fees waived when going this route.

You can also go to your county social service agency to get referrals to local health centers and nonprofits that may be able to help you. 

There are also resources to help with lowering your housing (rent or mortgage help), energy bills, phone bills, low cost auto insurance, financial planning help and more.  Let me know what you need help with the most right now and I can share more information.

Eligibility: You have to live in California and meet certain rules like income cut-offs based on household size (138% of the federal poverty level or lower, which is $36,777 for a household of 3). Even if your income is over the Medi-Cal limit, you could still get help paying for private health care through Covered California. You can qualify even if you are not a US citizen or national. 

How to apply: 
- Go in person to your county office (if you tell me your county, I can look this up for you) or online on BenefitsCal.com.
- To make the application faster, spend some time gathering these documents first, typically 1 or 2 in each category: 
    - Identity: birth certificate, driver's license, SSN, paycheck, US passport, military ID, etc. 
    - Immigration Status: INS documents, immigration papers/forms/cards, certificate of naturalization, etc. 
    - Proof you live in California: driver's license, check stub, rent/mortgage receipt, utility bill, etc.
    - Money you earn: check stubs for last 30 days, statement from employer, last year's tax return, bank statement for direct deposit 
    - Other income: benefit check, copies of child support checks, alimony, award letters 
    - Resources: bank statements showing savings / checkings accounts, mortgage statements, vehicle registration, etc. 
    - Additional proof of coverage: information about any job related health insurance that is open to your or your family, policy numbers of any current plans 

How long does it take? 
- California must decide on your case within 45 days. You may hear back sooner. If you have a disability it may take up to 90 days (depending on how quickly you submit documents and doctors submit records. 
- To **speed up the process**, tell your county office that you have an urgent medical or dental need. This can be a serious illness or also if you are pregnant. Your wife's health condition may count so be sure to share details about it when you apply. 

Using and Keeping your coverage: 
- If approved, you'll get a Benefits Identification Card (BIC) in the mail. You can start using Medi-Cal right away. To get all benefits, you may need to pick a Medi-Cal health plan. Your county will mail you details about plans and how to sign up. 
- If anything changes in your situation like moving, income amount, number of people in your home, pregnancy, or marital status, you need to update your application within **10 days**. 
- You have to renew your benefits every year on the anniversary of your enrollment in Medi-Cal. The county may automatically renew you or you may need to provide additional information if not. They will mail you a letter telling you what they need. Log in to your account to find out your renewal date. It's good to put a reminder in your calendar a year from when get approved as a reminder. 

### Covered California (state-based exchange from the Affordable Care Act)
Covered California offers financial help to lower the cost you pay for private health insurance plans. If you don't end up qualifying for Medi-Cal, this is another great option. 
Eligibility: Anyone can apply for Covered California if you are a California resident and have satisfactory immigration status. Financial help is available for people who are within 138% to 400% of the federal poverty level. DACA recipients do not qualify. People who are not lawfully present do not qualify. People over 65 usually do not as well (they are Medicare eligible). 

How to apply: Applying online is fastest (takes about 30 minutes) on coveredca.com. You can also get free help locally from a certified enroller or apply by phone (takes about 1 hour). You can also complete a paper application and mail it in but processing may take a bit longer. 

Gathering these documents ahead of time can make the application process go faster: 
Covered California compares information you put in your application with government data sources. If the data does not match, Covered California will need additional documents from you such as the following: proof of income, SSN, identity, citizenship / immigration status, proof of lack of minimum essential health coverage (this can be a certificate from an insurance company showing end date of your previous coverage, an employer statement saying they no longer offer this kind of health coverage, etc.). For the other categories, the types of documents you'd need are similar to Medi-Cal, but let me know if you want me to pull specific document types that could work. 

Keeping your benefits: 
You must report any changes in your life situation to (for example, address, family size, income) within 30 days. Renewal is in the fall of each year and goes to the end of the calendar year. You'll get notified by Covered California when it's time. 

### COBRA insurance 
You may have been offered temporary COBRA insurance, which is usually offered by your employer to help you keep your health plan after getting let go or getting reduced hours. You can still apply for Medi-Cal or Covered California even if you have a COBRA plan. 

COBRA is another temporary option for health coverage. It applies to most private companies with 20 or more employees. It requires that the employer's group health insurance plan continues after qualifying life events such as: Termination of reduction in employee hours and more. 
How long do COBRA benefits last? 
This depends on the qualifying life event. Some times this is 36 months or 3 years. If you are on COBRA because your employer reduced your hours or terminated your job, you could receive COBRA for 18 months or 1.5 years. 
Eligibility for COBRA: 
- Your group health plan must be covered by COBRA
- A qualifying life event must occur 
- You must be a qualified beneficiary for the event. 
How to Get COBRA: 
- Your employer notifies your health plan when a qualifying life event happens.
- Keep an eye out for an election notice from the health plan - you will have 60 days to respond to it. 
- If you accept the COBRA coverage, your employer may pay some or the full amount of your monthly premium. 
If you have questions, you should contact your employer's health insurance plan administrator. 

### Help with Medical Bills
There are also options for help with medical bills even if you don't have insurance or are under-insured (you have healthcare needs that are not covered by your plan): 
After applying for Medicaid (Medi-Cal) and ACA Marketplace (Covered California), and you still need help covering health care costs, you can still get help through the following: 
- Charity care: in most cases, you can apply through the doctor office or hospital where you are seeking medical treatment. Take these steps: 
    - First, ask for a copy of the hosital or provider's financial assistance policy. 
    - Fill out the application with information about your income and expenses 
    - Ask questions about the process like how long it will take to process your application and what happens to your bill in the meantime
    - Notify debt collectors if they are trying to collect and ask them to pause while that is pending 
    - Follow up with the hospital / provider and its billing department about your application's status as needed. 
- Medicare has several savings and extra help options - but this only applies if you are Medicare eligible - usually 65 years or older 
- Debt management: Get on a payment schedule with a credit counselor. You make an account with the credit counseling organization and then pay off your debt as you deposit money. You may get lower interest rates and certain fees waived when going this route. 
- Prescription costs: You can contact the pharmaceutical companies that make your drugs or devices and ask about low cost options, samples or discounts. See if your drug has a generic version - this is the same formulation but with a different brand that is usually more affordable. You can also go to your county social service agency to get referrals to local health centers and nonprofits that may be able to help you. 
 
## Food Help
- If you need food now, you can go to your local county food bank or call first to see if you qualify for help:  https://www.cdss.ca.gov/food-banks 
- Apply for SNAP (food stamps) - called CalFresh in California. If eligible, you can get monthly help paying for groceries. It can take 30 days to hear back, but you can ask for a faster decision (expedited review). 
- Your household size is based on how many people you live and buy/make food with. If you can tell me more about how much your household makes, and how old everyone is, I can check how likely you are to qualify. For a household of 3, you can't make more than $4,304 before taxes a month. The only way to know for sure if you are eligible is to apply. 
- You can apply on BenefitsCal.com or go to your county office. Online chat support is available M-F 9am to 4pm PT. 
- Your county will call within 1-2 weeks for an interview and will let you know within 30 days if you're approved. 
- If approved, you will get your EBT card for groceries within 10 days. It gets refilled monthly. 
- Documents you need: copy of your ID, proof of any income, proof of immigration status (for non-citizens) within 30 days of applying. Other optional documents could increase you benefit amount like proof of housing expenses, child support, child or dependent care, being older (60+) or disabled with medical expenses. 

## CalWORKs / TANF / Cash Aid
- CalWORKs helps with cash to pay for rent, housing, food, clothing, medical payments, and utilities for families with at least one child in the home. If your daughter is under 18, you may qualify. Some families also qualify for ongoing help and receive money each month to help pay for housing, food and other necessary expenses. The sooner you apply, the sooner you'll hear back. 
- Services vary by county but in addition to cash aid can include housing support, employment help, child care, education, mental health, substance use support, and domestic abuse support 
- The amount of help you could get depends on your family's income, household size, and any special needs. 
- If approved for cash aid, the monthly amount gets added to your EBT card (same as CalFresh) or can be directly deposited into a bank account. 
To Apply: 
You can apply at any Social Services office in the county you live in (https://www.cdss.ca.gov/county-offices) or apply online at BenefitsCal.com.
Once you have all your documents, applying should take 30-60 minutes. I can also provide a more detailed list of the documents you would need, but generally: ID, proof you live in California, money you recieve, expenses. 
Key Dates: your county will tell you the kinds of change you need to report and by when, but usually within 10 days.  To keep your benefits, your county will also reach out once a year but each program has different requirements. 

## Unemployment Benefits 
- What is it? Temporary income when you lose your job (or had hours reduced) through no fault of your own. 
- How much can I get? You get from $40 to $450 each week, depending on how much you earned in the past 18 months. EDD has an Unemployment Benefit Calculator to help you estimate how much you might get before you apply. 
- How long does it take to hear back? It takes about three weeks to process your benefit application and make the first payment. 
- You may also be able to attend school or training while receiving unemployment benefits. Learn more about California Training Benefits here: https://edd.ca.gov/en/unemployment/Eligible_Training_Types_for_CTB/ 
- Am I eligible? You need to have all of the following to get unemployment benefits: Social Security number, authorization to work in the US (if not a US citizen), have earned a minimum amount of money over the past 18 months (called base period), be totally or partially unemployed through no fault of your own, and be physically able to, available for and looking for work each week and ready / willing to accept work right away
- What documents you need to make applying faster: 
    - Personal Information (SSN, photo ID, other identity documentation like a W2 or bill)
    - Past 18 Months of Employment Information (Employer names, mailing and physical addresses, dates worked, total income before taxes and deductions (gross wages), hours worked, and how you were paid (e.g., weekly or monthly)
    - Most Recent Employer Information (Employer name, address, and phone number and your immediate supervisor, date you last worked, and total income before taxes and deductions (gross wages) in the last week (Sun - Sat) you worked
    - Reason you aren't working or had your hours cut (note: if you voluntarily quit or were fired / let go for misconduct, you may not be able to get benefits) 
    - Citizenship (if non-US citizen, you’ll need your USCIS document, such as your Permanent Resident Card, Employment Authorization Card, or Refugee Travel Document) 
    - There are additional documents if you worked in federal government or military service in the last 18 months (Notice to Federal Employee About Unemployment Insurance, Standard Form 8 and DD214 Member Copy 4 respectively). 

- How to apply and what to expect? 
**Step 1:** Get all the information and documents above together. 
**Step 2:** Apply online on California's EDD website, call by phone 1-800-300-5616 M-F 8am to 5pm PT or apply by fax or mail 
**Step 3:** After you apply, you have 21 days to sign up for and upload your resume to CalJOBS. 
**Step 4:** Review Benefit Documents - 2 weeks after you apply, California EDD may ask for more information. They will also send you key documents about your benefits. 
**Step 5:** Certify for Benefits - you need to answer some basic questions every 2 weeks to tell EDD that you are still unemployed but actively looking. Keep an eye out for an email / mail from EDD when it's time. It's fastest to certify online through myEDD, but you can also call 1-866-333-4606 for English and Spanish or by mail (your payments may take longer by mail)
**Step 6:** Receive Your First Payment - generally takes 3 weeks after you submit your application up to getting your first payment. You can get it by direct deposit, debit card or mailed check. Note, there is a one week waiting period on your claim before getting paid. Your first certification will usually include one week unpaid waiting period and one week of payment if you meet eligibility for both weeks. 
**Step 7:** Keep Certifying - you must do this step 5 every 2 weeks to keep your benefits 
**Step 8:** End Your Benefits: your benefit year ends 12 months after the start date of your first claim. You will need to re-apply if you still meet eligibility criteria. 
 
## Help Finding a Job
California also offers a lot of options finding a new job: 
- For workshops and services to improve your resume and develop job search skills, see EDD's website for more: https://edd.ca.gov/en/jobs/ 
- If you apply for unemployment benefits, you also have to create an account with CalJOBS and can find: education and training programs, customize job searches, create different resumes, research employers, set up alerts, apply directly to any openings, and there is a mobile app to make things easier too. 
- America's Job Center of California (AJCC) also gives free job and training services. You can use the American Job Center Finder to find a AJCC near you. You can also attend job fairs and career workshops with the AJCC to help grow your network. You can also join local or virtual workshops on common topics like how to use CalJOBS, how to search for jobs, and resume tips and interview coaching. 

## Financial Planning and Debt Management 
A budget is a roadmap to plan your finances and keep track of where your money goes. Budgeting is a helpful tool whether you’re working hard to make ends meet or if you have some extra income and want to adjust your saving goals. It will help you see where you spend your money and how you might spend money differently.

To make a budget:
- Gather your bills (utilities, insurance, etc.) and pay stubs.
- Collect receipts for things you typically spend money on like groceries, entertainment, transportation, clothing, and everyday expenses.
- Add up all of your paychecks and any other income. Subtract your expenses from that.

When you’re done, look for things in your budget you might be able to change so you have more money left over each month. Your goal is to stop adding to your debt, and also to pay down the debt you already have, if you can. You can find information about budgeting and money management online, at your public library, and in bookstores. 

If you’re behind on your bills, don’t wait to call the creditors you owe money to. Do it before a debt collector gets involved. Tell your creditors what’s going on, and try to work out a new payment plan with lower payments you can manage.

Let me know if you’d like more information about debt management such as what to do when having trouble paying a car loan, student loans, mortgage, or credit card debt. I can also give you more information about credit counseling organizations if you’d like more one-on-one support. 

## Another free resource is EarnIn.com, go here to get help with the following: 
- Sign up and link your bank account to be able to access your paycheck ahead of time. No interest or credit check - just tip what you think is fair and can afford at the time. Get money in your account in 1-3 business days or in minutes for a small fee. Any amount you use are then deducted when your pay check goes to your bank. If you qualify, you can get up to an average of $85 as a daily max. The amount can vary from $0 to $300 depending on your paycheck amount and other factors. 

EarnIn also provides free access to calculators to help with managing budget, rent, personal loans, credit card payoff, student loan, auto loan, and mortgage loan payments. 

California also offers help paying for rent / mortgage, phone bills, and low cost auto insurance. Would you like to learn more?
